key_insight: TIDER improves long-term agent memory retrieval by locating relevant time windows so temporally mismatched but semantically similar memories do not crowd out target evidence.
engineering_relevance: Memory systems for long-horizon LLM agents can combine temporal and semantic retrieval to better distinguish similar events occurring at different times.
method: Train a lightweight 1.7B temporal interval locator with reinforcement learning and composite rewards derived from answer supervision.
Retrieve candidates through separate temporal-window and semantic channels.
Merge candidates and rerank them by proximity to the predicted time windows.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports state-of-the-art accuracy of 61.52% on LifeBench (+8.82%) and 78.96% on LoCoMo (+3.66%).
watch_item: Incorrectly localized time windows could weaken retrieval; the abstract does not report robustness to ambiguous temporal cues or inference overhead.
paper_title: RL-Guided Temporal Localization for Dual-Channel Retrieval in Long-Horizon Agent Memory
